strings.why.laku-noc.7lx6ow: Laku noć means "good night". You say it when someone goes to sleep.
strings.why.dobra-vecer.1o3pkot: Dobra večer means "good evening". You use it after the sun goes down.
strings.why.dovidenja.tioegr: Doviđenja means "goodbye". It is not a greeting.
strings.g-hello-mcq.prompt: It is the morning. Which greeting do you use?
strings.g-hello-mcq.dyk: Among friends, a short "Bok" works at any time of day: it means both "hi" and "bye".
strings.g-hello-typed.prompt: How do you say "Good day" in Croatian?
strings.g-hello-typed.explanation: "Dobar dan" is the standard polite greeting during the day.
strings.g-evening-typed.prompt: How do you say "Good evening" in Croatian?
strings.g-evening-typed.explanation: "Dobra večer" is used from the evening on. Careful with the letter č: in Croatian it is a different letter from c.
strings.g-evening-typed.dyk: Croatian has five letters English does not: č, ć, š, ž and đ.
strings.g-hello-match.prompt: Match each English greeting with its Croatian phrase.
strings.g-hello-match.explanation: Dobro jutro (morning), Dobar dan (day), Dobra večer (evening) and the casual Bok.
strings.g-hello-card.explanation: "Bok" is the casual greeting and goodbye among friends.
strings.why.dobro-jutro.1e7xexp: Dobro jutro means "good morning" and is used before about ten o'clock.
strings.why.laku-noc.1j0wp2w: Laku noć means "good night" and is said at bedtime.
strings.g-hello-listen.prompt: Listen to the clip and choose the greeting you hear.
strings.g-hello-listen.explanation: The clip says "Dobar dan". (In this test course the sound is a placeholder tone, not speech: a real voice comes with text-to-speech.)
strings.why.dobro-jutro.18d99q8: Dobro jutro means "good morning": the wrong time of day.
strings.why.bok.112vx4f: Bok is a casual "hi" or "bye". It does not wish anyone a good night.
strings.why.dovidenja.14apk7o: Doviđenja means "goodbye". To wish a good night you say Laku noć.
strings.g-bye-mcq.prompt: You are going to bed. What do you say?
strings.g-bye-typed.prompt: How do you say "Goodbye" in Croatian?
strings.g-bye-match.prompt: Match each English phrase with its Croatian phrase.
strings.g-bye-match.explanation: Doviđenja (goodbye), Laku noć (good night), Do sutra (see you tomorrow), Vidimo se (see you).
strings.g-bye-card.explanation: "Laku noć" is what you say when someone is going to sleep.
strings.g-greet-ws.prompt: Find the Croatian words in the grid.
strings.g-greet-ws.explanation: Bok, jutro, dan, večer, noć, hvala and molim are all words from this unit. The grid writes č and ć as plain c.
strings.g-name-mcq.opt.name: Your name
strings.g-name-mcq.why.where: Where you are from is asked with "Odakle si?".
strings.g-name-mcq.why.age: Age is asked with "Koliko imaš godina?".
strings.g-name-mcq.prompt: A new friend asks "Kako se zoveš?" What do they want to know?
strings.g-name-mcq.explanation: "Kako se zoveš?" means "What is your name?" (literally "How are you called?").
strings.g-name-typed.prompt: Say "My name is Ana" in Croatian.
strings.g-name-typed.explanation: "Zovem se Ana" means "My name is Ana".
strings.g-name-typed.dyk: Croatian says "I call myself Ana": "zovem se" is literally "I am called".
strings.g-name-cloze.prompt: Fill the gap: "My name is Ana."
strings.g-name-cloze.explanation: "Zovem se Ana": the little word "se" belongs to the verb.
strings.g-name-match.l.ti: What is your name? (to a friend)
strings.g-name-match.prompt: Match each English phrase with its Croatian phrase.
strings.g-name-match.explanation: Zovem se Ana (my name is Ana), Drago mi je (nice to meet you) and the two ways to ask a name: Kako se zoveš? (to a friend) and Kako se zovete? (to a stranger or an older person).
strings.g-name-order.explanation: First a greeting and the question, then the answer and the question back, then the reply, and last "Drago mi je".
strings.g-name-listen.prompt: Listen to the clip and type the sentence you hear.
strings.g-name-listen.explanation: The clip says "Zovem se Ana". (In this test course the sound is a placeholder tone, not speech: a real voice comes with text-to-speech.)
strings.g-name-card.explanation: "Drago mi je" is what you say when you meet someone.
strings.why.zovem-se-ivan.1xuvjg8: That answers "Kako se zoveš?" (what is your name), not "Kako si?".
strings.why.dovidenja-dot.1wjpzon: That is goodbye, not an answer about how you are.
strings.why.laku-noc-dot.ovsgn6: Good night is said at bedtime. It does not answer the question.
strings.g-how-mcq.prompt: A friend asks "Kako si?" Which reply fits?
strings.g-how-mcq.explanation: "Kako si?" means "How are you?". A natural answer is "Dobro sam, hvala." ("I am fine, thank you.").
strings.g-how-typed.prompt: Reply to "Kako si?": "I am fine, thank you."
strings.g-how-typed.explanation: "Dobro sam, hvala." means "I am fine, thank you." You can add "A ti?" to ask back.
strings.why.molim.1fukrer: Molim means "please" or "you are welcome". You say it when you offer something or answer "Hvala", not when you receive.
strings.g-polite-mcq.prompt: Someone hands you a coffee. What do you say?
strings.g-polite-typed.prompt: How do you say "Thank you" in Croatian?
strings.g-polite-typed.explanation: "Hvala" means "thank you". You will also hear "hvala lijepa" (thank you very much).
strings.g-polite-match.prompt: Match each English phrase with its Croatian phrase.
strings.g-polite-match.explanation: Hvala (thank you), Molim (please, you are welcome), Oprostite (excuse me, polite) and Oprosti (sorry, to a friend).
strings.why.kako-si.1p3oveg: "Kako si?" is informal ("ti"): for friends, family and children.
strings.why.kako-se-zoves.1e423fs: That asks "What is your name?" in the informal way, and not how they are.
strings.g-formal-mcq.prompt: You meet your teacher. How do you politely ask how they are?
strings.g-formal-mcq.explanation: With one person you do not know well, or someone older, you use the polite "Vi": "Kako ste?".
strings.g-formal-mcq.dyk: The polite "Vi" is written with a capital letter in letters and messages: "Hvala Vam".
strings.g-formal-sort.prompt: Sort the phrases: friendly (ti) or polite (Vi)?
strings.g-formal-sort.explanation: With friends, family and children you say "ti": Kako si? Kako se zoveš? Hvala ti. With a stranger or an older person you say "Vi": Kako ste? Kako se zovete? Hvala Vam.
strings.g-formal-typed.prompt: Politely ask your teacher "How are you?"
strings.g-formal-typed.explanation: "Kako ste?" is the polite way to ask "How are you?".
strings.g-formal-cloze.prompt: Fill the gap: "How are you?" (to your teacher)
strings.g-formal-cloze.explanation: "Kako ste?" is polite; "Kako si?" would be for a friend.
strings.g-formal-tf.why: Bok is a casual greeting among friends. A polite greeting for strangers is "Dobar dan".
strings.g-formal-tf.prompt: "Bok" is a formal greeting you can use with strangers.
strings.g-formal-tf.explanation: "Bok" is casual, for friends. With a stranger you say "Dobar dan".
strings.hr.unit.greetings.title: Greetings and goodbyes
strings.hr.unit.greetings.summary: Say hello and goodbye at every time of day.
strings.hr.unit.intro.title: Introducing yourself
strings.hr.unit.intro.summary: Say your name and ask how someone is.
strings.hr.unit.polite.title: Polite phrases: ti and Vi
strings.hr.unit.polite.summary: Say thank you and please, and choose between friendly and polite.
strings.hr.obj.obj-hello: Greet people at different times of the day.
strings.hr.obj.obj-name: Say your name and ask for someone’s name.
strings.hr.obj.obj-how: Ask how someone is and answer.
strings.hr.obj.obj-polite: Use the basic polite words: thank you, please and excuse me.
strings.hr.obj.obj-formal: Choose between the friendly "ti" and the polite "Vi".
strings.hr.asset.dobar-dan.alt: A placeholder tone (one long beep), not speech. It stands in for a recording of "Dobar dan" until text-to-speech is added.
strings.hr.asset.zovem-se.alt: A placeholder tone (three beeps), not speech. It stands in for a recording of "Zovem se Ana" until text-to-speech is added.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.title: A café in Zagreb
strings.rp.sc.cafe.setting: Ana works in a small café in Zagreb. You walk in three times today: in the morning, at noon and in the evening.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l2.help: Hint: it is the morning, and jutro means morning.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l3.tr: I am Ana. This is my café.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l6.help: Hint: she greets you in the middle of the day, and dan means day.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l7.tr: You again! It is evening already.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l8.help: Hint: večer means evening. Mind the č.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l9.tr: I am closing the café now. I am going home.
strings.rp.sc.cafe.l10.help: Hint: it is what you say when someone leaves. Mind the đ.
strings.rp.sc.school.title: A language school in Split
strings.rp.sc.school.setting: Your first day at a language school in Split. Luka sits next to you and Marija is the teacher.
strings.rp.sc.school.l3.help: Hint: Zovem se ... means "My name is ...".
strings.rp.sc.school.l6.help: Hint: you want to say that you are fine, and to thank him.
strings.rp.sc.school.l7.tr: Great! Say it as a full sentence.
strings.rp.sc.school.l8.help: Hint: Dobro sam means "I am well".
strings.rp.sc.school.l11.help: Hint: three words, and the first one is Zovem.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.title: At the hotel desk
strings.rp.sc.hotel.setting: You are staying in a hotel in Split. Your Croatian course is held here, and Marija, your teacher, stands at the desk.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l1.tr: Good day! Here you are, a coffee for you.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l2.help: Hint: someone hands you something. What do you say?
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l3.tr: You are welcome! I am Marija, your teacher.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l4.help: Hint: she is your teacher, so use the polite Vi.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l5.tr: I am well, thank you. This is your key.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l6.help: Hint: it is the word you said for the coffee.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l7.tr: You are welcome. Ask me once more.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l8.help: Hint: to a teacher you say Vi, so the verb is ste.
strings.rp.sc.hotel.l9.tr: I am well, thank you! See you tomorrow!
strings.rp.sc.final.title: The last evening
strings.rp.sc.final.setting: It is your last evening in Split. At the ferry quay you meet Ivan, the ferry officer, and your friends Luka and Marija come to say goodbye.
strings.rp.sc.final.l2.help: Hint: večer means evening. Mind the č.
strings.rp.sc.final.l4.help: Hint: Zovem se ... means "My name is ...".
strings.rp.sc.final.l5.tr: Nice to meet you. Here you are, a coffee for the road.
strings.rp.sc.final.l6.help: Hint: someone hands you something. What do you say?
strings.rp.sc.final.l8.help: Hint: you want to say that you are fine, and to thank him.
strings.rp.sc.final.l9.tr: Good evening! Ask me once more.
strings.rp.sc.final.l10.help: Hint: to a teacher you say Vi, so the verb is ste.
strings.rp.sc.final.l11.tr: The ship is leaving! I have to go.
strings.rp.sc.final.l12.help: Hint: it is what you say when someone leaves. Mind the đ.
strings.rp.w.dobar-dan.gloss: Good day (hello from late morning until evening)
